A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same K-Viscuit benchmark and human–VLM construction framework. The main text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and matchable, including v1 Appendices A–D and v2's added Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM evaluations, language and retrieval experiments, and a human study involving 20 Koreans and 14 non-Koreans.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds model evaluations, Korean-CVQA results, and human assessment of 80 generated answers. Table 5 separately identifies its VQAv2 scores as taken from model papers.

M1.justification: The four-stage construction framework, GPT-4-Turbo annotation inputs, appendix prompts, human verification, and retrieval procedure remain substantively unchanged. Renaming the pipeline and reframing verification around cultural subtleties do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on CVQA's Korean subset in Table 5; its VQAv2 comparison uses published scores. K-Viscuit retains the same 657 questions, ten categories, and cultural scope. Generative VQA was already explored in v1, so its expanded evaluation does not introduce a new task.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 add Molmo-7B-D, Llama-3.2-11B, and GPT-4o to the ten retained models. GPT-4o also joins the language and retrieval comparisons. Conversely, the reported human-subset comparison narrows from ten VLMs in v1 Figure 6 to GPT-4-Turbo and LLaVA-1.6-13B in v2 Figure 5, substantially revising comparator participation across experiments.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 adds a bounded evaluation protocol: randomly sample 80 Food questions, prompt LLaVA-1.6-13B without answer options, and have two native Korean evaluators classify responses as correct, hallucinated, or abstained. Existing multiple-choice, translation, retrieval, and 50-question human-study protocols remain as previously stated.

E4.justification: v1's exploration of generative-answer failures relied on two illustrative examples. v2 retains those examples and adds systematic human scoring of 80 responses, including a hallucination and abstention breakdown in Table 6. This substantially extends the evidence about weaknesses hidden by multiple-choice evaluation.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 5 introduces boxplots showing variation in human accuracy, whereas v1 Figure 6 displayed only human group averages alongside model bars. This adds distributional reporting, without adding documented repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Shared model scores remain unchanged, but new entries alter rankings: GPT-4o leads at 89.50%, while the previous leader Gemini-1.5-Pro remains at 81.58%. v2 adds CVQA scores and GPT-4o language/retrieval results. Human averages change from 72.1%/45.57% to 80.2%/47.0%, without an explanation of the revision. New Table 6 reports 29 correct, 34 hallucinated, and 17 abstained answers; its printed 36.35% correct conflicts with 29/80 and the text's 36.25%.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The new response categories constitute an empirical scoring rubric rather than a theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a semi-automated human–VLM framework, the K-Viscuit Korean cultural benchmark, and a performance gap between proprietary and open-source VLMs. The rewritten abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain these contributions and their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds a qualification about separating language from culture, reframes human verification as selecting cultural subtleties, and explicitly conditions retrieval benefits on document quality. It also interprets abstentions as recognizing missing information and narrows the human-performance discussion to GPT-4-Turbo. The existing manual-construction limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future dataset/code release promise with a dataset availability link and supplies the new free-form prompt and scoring instructions. It also documents romanization of terms lacking English equivalents. The explicit regenerate-if-all-candidates-fail instruction disappears from the main text, while the existing appendix prompts and original checkpoint details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on collaborative annotation, language–culture relationships, newer models, and cultural benchmarking, including Bartolo et al., Kamalloo et al., and Nayak et al. Appendix E adds a size-based positioning argument against the already-cited CVQA, reporting 657 K-Viscuit examples versus 290 Korean CVQA examples. The central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, construction description, discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting and compression. Terminology changes from pipeline to framework, and an Ethical Statement and Appendix E are added. These are substantial editorial changes despite retaining the main section sequence.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 7 are redrawn, and the human-evaluation display changes from model bars to human boxplots. Two result tables are added, existing comparison tables expand, and dataset examples and other displays move. The appendix prompt tables are retained and renumbered, rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 improves usefulness through broader model comparisons, Korean-CVQA evaluation, quantitative free-form error analysis, and dataset-access information. Human-score distributions and more qualified interpretations also strengthen reporting. The gains are limited by the new Table 6 percentage inconsistency and the absence of an explicitly matched 80-question multiple-choice comparison in Section 5.1. Overall, the added evidence modestly strengthens the retained benchmark contribution.
